messages:
keith: FYI — upstream advisory for a libssl bug that affects Alpine-based images: CVE-2028-4512. Reports of TLS1.3 session resumption causing handshake failures under certain server configs. We need a quick triage for our base images (api, workers, runtime).

maria: link? exploitability?

keith: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/CVE-2028-4512 (external link) — summary: non-authenticated client resumption can cause connection resets when specific session tickets are present. PoC limited but affects musl-linked OpenSSL builds (Alpine).

julia: Which of our images are FROM alpine:3.20? I have a rough inventory but should enumerate. off the top: api-base, worker-lite, sandbox-runtime.

devon: Quick decision call: do we rebuild a new alpine-based base image with updated openssl package, or attempt to hotpatch the package in place? Also: signing implications for Dedicated/Private customers (KMS).

keith: Proposed triage plan: 1) Determine exact impact surface (list images + runtime flags) 2) Build canary base images with patched OpenSSL 3) Run regression matrix: TLS handshake, replays, KV clients, long-lived connections 4) Canary rollout to Dedicated infra first (no external-facing prod) 5) Sign artifacts with KMS and publish provenance + revocation plan.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: noted. Will queue an internal canary pipeline when requested.

maria: KMS question: our hosted images are signed with Redwood central KMS. For Private installs we need to support customer-managed KMS keys. Does the signing flow change for emergency rollouts? Who owns key rotation?

anna: From sec side: RBAC rules we should enforce — only sec-release and eng-infra may trigger rebuild + signing. All sign actions must be audited. We'll add an approval step for emergency rollouts and require an incident justification field.

devon: Tests I plan to add to the pipeline: 
- openssl s_client TLS1.3 handshake + session resumption
- curl --http2 against local server with session tickets
- internal e2e harness for persistent connections (5m soak)
- smoke checks for musl vs glibc behavior (Alpine vs Ubuntu)
Snippets I used locally:```
# run s_client check
openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:443 -tls1_3 -sess_out sess.bin
openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:443 -tls1_3 -sess_in sess.bin
```

julia: Note: some runtime images are Ubuntu-based (glibc). We should parallel-track glibc/OpenSSL updates for those; don't assume Alpine-only. I can produce a mapping by EOD.

keith: Timeline suggestion: start triage now. Aim for an internal canary build by EOD tomorrow. Owners: devon -> canary build + pipeline, maria -> test harness & results collection, anna -> RBAC/signing policy + audit hooks, julia -> full image inventory including ubuntu/glibc variants. @devon please ack.

devon: ack. will spin up a branch and post pipeline id in this thread. Expect initial canary in ~18h.

ops-bot: pipeline #342 queued by devon (canary-base-rebuild). Estimated runtime: 25m.

keith: Good. A few operational notes:
- Add package pins in our baseimage manifests to avoid accidental rollbacks to vulnerable packages.
- Include provenance metadata (build commit, package versions, KMS signature key id).
- Document rollback steps: re-tag previous signed image, update routing for Dedicated pools, record audit justification.

maria: I'll add entries to remediation runbook: image.build, image.sign, rollout.trigger should all produce audit events. Also include verification checklist for Private customers (KMS key ARN acceptance, HSM-backed signing).

julia: I'll drop the full inventory file (image -> base -> openssl version) in #eng-releases by EOD. Will flag any images that are pinned to older musl/OpenSSL combos.

keith: Thanks — keep updates here. If tests show regressions we may need to fallback to: (a) revert to older package + additional mitigations, or (b) use ubuntu base for affected components until upstream patch stabilizes.

maria: noted. tagging the thread with :triage: and will prepare comms for SRE/Support if customer impact looks likely.

devon: pipeline #342 started. I’ll post logs when first artifacts are available.

ops-bot: pipeline #342 status: running

keith: appreciate the quick turnaround. One last ask: include a small smoke-check harness that runs in CI against the canary image and writes a pass/fail artifact into S3 so audit can pick it up.

maria: on it.

(devon will follow up with pipeline logs and artifacts)
